guide.title: Iceland  : 6 days itinerary
guide.description:
A six-day road trip through Iceland is a journey into raw and untamed beauty,
where landscapes shift dramatically from waterfalls to glaciers, volcanic  fi elds,
and black-sand shores. Each day on the road reveals a new wonder, o ff ering the
freedom to explore nature’s extremes at your own pace.

data.name: Ke fl avik International Airport
data.description: Tips - Rent the car at the terminal, 4x4 otherwise I'll mark the places where it’s not advisable for you to go.

data.name: Krónan
data.description: Stop by a supermarket in the capital and get ready for the journey Tips - Bonus is the cheapest market but has fewer supplies. Kronan is a great compromise.

data.name: Thingvellir National Park
data.description: Thingvellir National Park, a UNESCO site, features stunning geology and history, including the Althing, the world's oldest parliament, founded in 930 AD.

data.name: Kerid Crater
data.description: Kerid Crater, a stunning volcanic formation in Iceland, features a vibrant blue lake surrounded by steep red slopes. Its unique beauty draws nature lovers and photographers alike, o ff ering breathtaking views and geological intrigue. Tips - Parking 4€

data.name: Geysir Hot Springs
data.description: Geysir Hot Springs, nestled in Haukadalur Valley, features the famous Strokkur geyser, which erupts every few minutes, reaching heights of 30 meters (98 feet). This geothermal marvel, rich in colorful mineral deposits and history, has captivated visitors since the 13th century, giving rise to the term 'geyser' globally.

data.name: Gullfoss Falls
data.description: Gullfoss Falls, situated in southwestern Iceland, is a breathtaking natural wonder, famed for its dramatic two- tiered drop of 32 meters (105 feet). Part of the Golden Circle, it o ff ers stunning views and accessible paths, making it a must-visit destination year-round for those seeking nature's awe-inspiring beauty. Tips - Raincoat mandatory if you don't want to get wet

data.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin)
data.description: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin), Iceland's oldest geothermal spa, invites relaxation in warm, mineral-rich waters amid stunning landscapes. Established in 1891, it o ff ers a serene escape with natural hot springs and picturesque views. Tips - 30€ p.p - If you want to save money, wait for free spots

data.name: Skyggnir Bed and Breakfast
data.description: Skyggnir Bed and Breakfast, established in 1993, provides a delightful escape in Fludir, Iceland, featuring unique rooms and easy access to Golden Circle attractions.

data.name: Haifoss
data.description: Haifoss, one of Iceland's tallest waterfalls, boasts breathtaking beauty in the highlands, rewarding adventurous visitors with serene surroundings and stunning vistas. Tips - Only if you have a 4x4 car - Often not feasible in winter

data.name: Sigoldufoss
data.description: Sigoldufoss, nestled along the Fjallabaksleið Nyrðri road, captivates with its vibrant blue waters reminiscent of nearby craters. Accessible by standard vehicles, it o ff ers a paradise- like canyon view, making it a hidden gem near a power dam. Tips - Only if you have a 4x4 car - Often not feasible in winter

data.name: Seljalandsfoss
data.description: Seljalandsfoss, a stunning 60-meter waterfall in Iceland, captivates visitors with its unique ability to walk behind the cascade. Surrounded by lush greenery, it’s part of the Seljalandsfoss Nature Reserve, drawing nature lovers and adventurers alike to its breathtaking beauty. Tips - Parking 7€

data.name: Gljúfrabúi
data.description: Gljúfrabúi is a stunning hidden waterfall tucked away in a narrow canyon in Iceland. Just a short walk from Seljalandsfoss, its serene pool and lush surroundings o ff er a unique experience, making it a perfect spot for nature lovers and photographers alike. Tips - Exactly opposite the previous waterfalls, same parking lot.

data.name: Skógafoss
data.description: Skógafoss, a breathtaking 60-meter waterfall in South Iceland, o ff ers stunning views, rainbows, and nearby hiking trails for nature enthusiasts. Tips - Parking 7€

data.name: Dyrholaey
data.description: Dyrhólaey, meaning "the hill island with the door hole," near Vík, features a historic archway, stunning coastal views, and seasonal pu ffi n sightings, with accessible viewpoints for breathtaking landscapes.

data.name: Reynisfjara Beach
data.description: Reynisfjara Beach, Iceland Strong ocean currents and intense easterly winds have removed much of the sand at this famous site, leaving the iconic basalt columns directly exposed to the waves. Tips - Parking 7€ What The Heck Is Happening To Reynisfjara Beach? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9JnyGXc-Kuc Vik South Region, Iceland Vik, or Vík í Mýrdal, is a picturesque village in South Iceland, renowned for its black sand beaches and stunning natural landscapes. Tips - Well-stocked city for shopping

data.name: The Barn
data.description: Norðurfoss, Vik, Iceland +3548617375 The Barn is a contemporary hotel near Vik, Iceland, featuring private rooms, a communal kitchen, and easy access to Reynisfjara Beach and Dyrhólaey. Tips - Stay 2 nights here.

data.name: Katla Ice Cave
data.description: Embark on an unforgettable 2-hour adventure exploring the breathtaking crystal ice caves of Vatnajokull Glacier, equipped with necessary gear and expert guidance. Tips - 210€ p.p. - Hiking shoes - Be careful to book the excursion that departs from Vik. You can choose either this excursion or the largest glacier in Europe, link below. (Meeting point after the Svartifoss waterfalls, in the early afternoon) Skaftafell: Vatnajökull experience https://www.getyourguide.it/parco-nazionale-del-vatnajokull-l2246/skaftafell-escursione-in-picco lo-gruppo-sul-ghiacciaio-vatnajokull-facile-t30308?ranking_uuid=889fd57c-7266-47c2-b3ce-a44 c9afd242f&date_from=2026-05-13 Cheaper, both are worth it. You don’t have time for both, you’ll have to decide.

data.name: Fjaðrárgljúfur
data.description: Fjaðrárgljúfur is a stunning canyon in southeast Iceland, stretching 2 kilometers and reaching depths of 100 meters. With its mossy cli ff s and winding river, it’s a favorite spot for hikers and photographers, showcasing Iceland's unique natural beauty. Tips - Parking 7€

data.name: Svartifoss
data.description: Svartifoss, or 'Black Fall', is a breathtaking waterfall in Vatnajökull National Park, Iceland, famous for its black basalt columns and stunning natural beauty, attracting nature lovers and photographers alike. Tips - 1h15 minutes round trip - Parking 7€

data.name: Mulagljufur Canyon
data.description: Mulagljufur Canyon, nestled in Vatnajökull National Park, Iceland, showcases dramatic cli ff s and lush greenery. This breathtaking area attracts hikers with its vibrant summer fl ora and picturesque trails, and is conveniently located near the renowned Skaftafell Nature Reserve.

data.name: Diamond Beach
data.description: Diamond Beach, adjacent to Jokulsarlon Glacier Lagoon, captivates with its sparkling icebergs on black sands. This striking contrast enchants visitors and serves as a gateway to explore Iceland's breathtaking natural wonders. Tips - Parking 7€ - From the parking lot, you can reach both the lagoon (you can see the seals) and the beach. 2½ hours to get back to Vik

data.name: Seljavallalaug Swimming Pool
data.description: Seljavallalaug Swimming Pool, Iceland's oldest pool since 1923, features warm spring water and breathtaking mountain views, making it a serene nature retreat. Tips - First free option (less crowded) - Remember to take a shower before entering.

data.name: Caves of Hella
data.description: The Caves of Hella, a hidden gem in Iceland, boast mesmerizing rock formations and geological wonders, perfect for exploration, photography, and a serene nature escape. The Old Dairy Food Hall - Mjólkurbúið

data.name: Mathöll
data.description: The Old Dairy Food Hall, or Mjólkurbúið Mathöll, is a lively dining spot in Selfoss, Iceland, featuring eight eateries and a wine bar, all set in a charming 1929 dairy building that celebrates Icelandic culinary heritage. Tips - An idea for lunch or even for having a drink.

data.name: Sunnumörk
data.description: Sunnumörk, located in Hveragerði, Iceland, is a mesmerizing destination known for its geothermal wonders. With natural hot springs and mud pots, it o ff ers stunning hiking trails and scenic views. The warm waters are said to have healing properties, making it an ideal spot for relaxation amidst nature. Tips - You can see the two tectonic plates through the glass in the  fl oor.

data.name: Reykjadalur Hot Spring Thermal River
data.description: Reykjadalur Hot Spring Thermal River is a stunning natural haven in Iceland's South Region. This popular hiking spot features scenic trails leading to its warm thermal waters, perfect for unwinding amidst breathtaking landscapes after a day of adventure. Tips - Second free option (more crowded)

data.name: Hvammsvik Hot Springs
data.description: If you're willing to pay €60, these thermal baths are worth every penny. Reykjavik Capital Region, Iceland Reykjavik, Iceland's capital, boasts breathtaking landscapes and cultural treasures. Discover iconic sites, relax in the Blue Lagoon, and enjoy the enchanting Northern Lights. Tips - Check the guide for the city (day 6)

data.name: Geldingadalir Volcano
data.description: Geldingadalir Volcano, located on the Reykjanes Peninsula, captivated visitors with its 2021 eruption, creating breathtaking lava  fi elds and scenic hiking trails. Tips - It's worth it if the volcano erupts, or if it is something that particularly interests you - Go in the dark hours

data.name: Loft - HI Hostel
data.description: Loft - HI Hostel is a lively and contemporary accommodation in downtown Reykjavik, Iceland. With a welcoming vibe and superb facilities, it features diverse room options, a communal lounge, a kitchen, and a rooftop terrace with breathtaking city and mountain views.

data.name: Ytri Tunga
data.description: Ytri Tunga, on Iceland's Snæfellsnes Peninsula, boasts stunning black sand beaches, diverse wildlife, including seals, and breathtaking views of the Snæfellsjökull glacier—ideal for nature enthusiasts.

data.name: Kirkjufell
data.description: Kirkjufell, located near Grundarfjörður in Iceland's West Region, is an iconic mountain known for its distinct shape and picturesque surroundings. Often photographed with the nearby Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall, it o ff ers breathtaking views and is a favorite spot for hikers and photographers alike. Tips - Parking 7€

data.name: Saxhóll Crater
data.description: Saxhóll Crater, a prominent volcanic cone in the Snæfellsnes Peninsula, invites visitors to hike its rugged terrain for breathtaking views of mountains and the Atlantic, showcasing Iceland's rich geological heritage. Tips - Parking 7€

data.name: Svörtuloft Lighthouse
data.description: Svörtuloft Lighthouse, perched on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula, is a breathtaking maritime beacon o ff ering panoramic views, dramatic cli ff s, and access to black sand beaches, showcasing Iceland's untamed natural beauty. Tips - Only if you have a 4x4 car

data.name: Skarðsvík Beach
data.description: Skarðsvík Beach, situated on the northwestern tip of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula, boasts golden sands and turquoise waters, reminiscent of Mediterranean shores. Surrounded by striking volcanic landscapes, it’s essential to visit during low tide for safety due to strong currents.

data.name: The Freezer Hostel & Culture Center
data.description: The Freezer Hostel & Culture Center, situated in Hellissandur on Iceland's stunning Snaefellsnes Peninsula, occupies a repurposed  fi sh processing factory. It features themed dorms, private apartments, and a lively atmosphere with cultural events, plus easy access to hiking and  fi shing in nearby Snaefellsjokull National Park.
